SECTION VI
THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN LOCAL SHORT-TERM USES OF MAN'S ENVIRONMENT AND
THE MAINTENANCE AND ENHANCEMENT OF LONG-TERM PRODUCTIVITY
The cumulative long-term effect of the many aspects of this project is to continue the present use of the various neighborhoods while making them more desirable to live in and preventing or reversing their decline into an unhealthful and/or unsafe condition.
In summary, the project requires the short-term commitment of energy and materials in order to maintain what are for the most part, long-term commitments of land use. These land uses are consistent with the City of San Jose General Plan.
The commitment of resources and expenditure of energy for the project is proposed at this time because current trends imply that ever-increasing amounts of materials and energy will be required to accomplish the same goals if the residential rehabilitation and public facilities programs are postponed to a later date.
